1004751.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Gandvík (“Gandvik”). The Old Norse name is traditionally analysed as gandr (“staff, magic staff; sorcery”) + vík (“bay, inlet”), and hence interpreted as “bay of magic” or “enchanted bay”.
The deeper origin is uncertain. Many scholars instead regard Gandvík as a folk-etymological adaptation of a Finnic place name, comparing Finnish Kantalahti, the name associated with the Kandalaksha Gulf. Under this interpretation, Finnish lahti (“bay, inlet”) was rendered as Old Norse vík (“bay, inlet”).
By surface analysis, gand (“magic, sorcery”) + vik (“bay, inlet”).

1005007.etyen:
Compound of bledning (“selection system”) + skog (“forest”), with linking -s- (“interfix”), literally “selection-system forest”.
The first element is the verbal noun bledning, from ble (“to select trees for felling”), ultimately from bleðja (“to pick off, gather”), related to blað (“leaf, blade”), from Proto-Germanic *bladą (“leaf, blade”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₃- (“to bloom, flower”). skog (“forest”) is inherited from skógr (“forest”), from Proto-Germanic *skōgaz (“forest, wood”), of uncertain deeper origin.
